nodes.label: CyberAlchemy
nodes.plain_language: A governed starting system for people and machines building complex systems together.
nodes.claim: CyberAlchemy combines human judgment, machine capabilities, knowledge, evidence, tests, feedback, and handoffs in one reviewable work system.
nodes.scope: The private CyberAlchemy product thesis; the CyberAlchemy v2 repository is modeled separately as an intended delivery form.
nodes.forbidden_collapse: Not a promoted definition, standalone release, public product claim, or proof that the product works.
open_questions: Which user group is the first product customer?

nodes.label: Human Participant
nodes.plain_language: The person who supplies intent, judgment, attention, tests, and explicit choices.
nodes.claim: The human remains able to see, challenge, and choose the next important move.
nodes.scope: People participating in a CyberAlchemy work loop.
nodes.forbidden_collapse: Not a passive approval button, a productivity score, or a source of inferred private state.

nodes.label: Machine Collaborator
nodes.plain_language: The agent or tool that can remember, recommend, prepare, test, route, or execute within an allowed boundary.
nodes.claim: Machine capabilities support the work loop without silently replacing human judgment or owner authority.
nodes.scope: Agents, tools, and automated capabilities used through CyberAlchemy.
nodes.forbidden_collapse: Not an autonomous owner and not permission for unreviewed execution.

nodes.label: Work Owner
nodes.plain_language: The person or route responsible for a decision, definition, lifecycle, or next action.
nodes.claim: Important work stays attached to an explicit owner instead of becoming unowned agent output.
nodes.scope: Domain, definition, lifecycle, and receiving owners participating in the work loop.
nodes.forbidden_collapse: Not one universal owner role and not an automatic authority grant.
open_questions: Should human participant, teammate, domain owner, and lifecycle owner remain separate actor types?

nodes.label: Complex Knowledge Work
nodes.plain_language: Work where meaning, evidence, decisions, software, tests, and handoffs must stay connected across time.
nodes.claim: CyberAlchemy is aimed at work that cannot be handled safely by one isolated agent, tool, document, or interface.
nodes.scope: System-building and other evidence-heavy knowledge work.
nodes.forbidden_collapse: Not all knowledge work and not a measured market segment.
open_questions: Which concrete work categories are in the first commercial or internal scope?

nodes.label: Disconnected Work Loop
nodes.plain_language: Intent, definitions, evidence, decisions, execution, tests, and handoffs live in separate places and stop informing each other.
nodes.claim: Disconnected tools shift coordination and memory work back to the person and make ownership or automation hard to see.
nodes.scope: The coordination problem addressed by the product thesis.

source_refs.selector: ## Why IDE Ergonomics Raises The Proposition

nodes.forbidden_collapse: Not a measured customer pain claim yet.
open_questions: Which forms of lost context or rework should be measured first?

nodes.label: Governed Human-Machine Integration
nodes.plain_language: People and machines work in one visible loop that fits the person, task, and moment while the person keeps control of important choices and every consequential action stays inside bounded, visible authority.
nodes.claim: CyberAlchemy commits to making complex human-machine work situated, reviewable, resumable, and actionable while preserving human agency, evidence, ownership, bounded authority, and proportionate governance.
nodes.scope: The committed CyberAlchemy product proposition represented by CA2-PRODUCT-THESIS-CYBERALCHEMY under the canonical Product Thesis meaning CAV2-D63. The artifact remains a candidate Spec representation.
nodes.forbidden_collapse: Not generic human-computer interaction, automatic execution, surveillance, a promoted definition, an implemented runtime, or validated product effectiveness.
open_questions: What product evidence is sufficient to validate the intended outcomes without changing the first-order commitment?

nodes.label: Governed Base Repository
nodes.plain_language: The intended downloadable starting repository with authority, ontology, inventory, definitions, rules, and promotion routes already visible.
nodes.claim: CyberAlchemy v2 is intended to become the base from which downstream systems can be built without reopening the same source and authority ambiguity.
nodes.scope: The intended delivery form, currently still inside the private parent repository.
nodes.forbidden_collapse: Not the human-machine integration value proposition and not an already extracted or released repository.
open_questions: When should the base repository be extracted?
Which parts may become public?

nodes.label: Governed Work Loop
nodes.plain_language: Sense the current work, choose a bounded next action, show the authority for any real consequence, act through its narrowest responsible route, test the result, preserve evidence, and hand off or repeat.
nodes.claim: The product coordinates human and machine contributions through a visible feedback loop that keeps harmless work lightweight and makes authority explicit when the consequence changes.
nodes.scope: The product-level work loop: sense, decide, route, act, test, preserve, hand off, and re-sense.
nodes.forbidden_collapse: Not one runtime workflow and not permission to execute every next action automatically.

nodes.label: Define Shared Meaning
nodes.plain_language: Read the goal and past evidence, find the required concepts, ask what is missing, and prepare checked definitions before Design.
nodes.claim: For each required concept, Define records reuse, specialization, a new candidate, or a visible open question, with evidence, scope, owner, and relationships.
nodes.scope: The public Invoke Define capability as one contributor to the private CyberAlchemy product thesis.

source_refs.selector: ## Journey 1: From Goal To A Definition Pack

nodes.forbidden_collapse: Not the complete CyberAlchemy product, canonical definition promotion, Design approval, implementation authority, or runtime execution.
open_questions: How should the same open question remain visible in both CLI and chat?

nodes.label: Resolve Bounded Language Context
nodes.plain_language: Prepare the exact language a person or agent may safely use for one bounded context and intended use.
nodes.claim: The capability resolves a source-digest-bound view of preferred expressions, concept identities, business, domain, and product meanings, dispositions, owners, evidence, realization candidates, relationship vocabulary, conflicts, and blocked uses without deciding unresolved meaning.
nodes.scope: Product-level Language capability used before or while Define works; request, view schema, cache, protocol, and implementation remain separate candidates.
nodes.owner_route: CyberAlchemy v2 Language Project owner plus bounded-context language owner
nodes.forbidden_collapse: Not a definition authority, automatic semantic inference, DomainSpec type selector, permission resolver, runtime implementation, or proof that a consumer used the language correctly.
open_questions: Which exact request and freshness contract should produce a Language Context View?
Which consumer evidence proves that applied bindings were preserved in the Definition Pack?

nodes.label: Language Context View
nodes.plain_language: A bounded, read-only view of the language that is usable for one context, intended use, and source epoch.
nodes.claim: The view identifies its language, context, intended use, exact sources and digests, usable bindings, unresolved conflicts, blocked uses, owners, and freshness so a consumer can reuse meaning without guessing.
nodes.scope: Product output of Resolve Bounded Language Context and input to Define; exact JSON shape and production runtime are not selected here.
nodes.owner_route: CyberAlchemy v2 Language Project owner plus consuming capability owner
nodes.forbidden_collapse: Not a copied canonical registry, accepted Definition Pack, authority envelope, selected open realization, mutable session state, or proof of semantic correctness.
open_questions: What is the minimum view shape that remains useful to agents and deterministic to validate?

nodes.label: Definition Pack
nodes.plain_language: A structured set of candidate definitions and open questions that Design can read, including the exact bounded language consulted by Define.
nodes.claim: The pack keeps each required concept, decision, evidence link, scope, owner, relationship, and unresolved question together and preserves the Language Context View identity, digest, source epoch, and applied binding references.
nodes.scope: The product-level output of Define; exact file and runtime contracts remain owned by Invoke.

source_refs.selector: The Definition Pack preserves the identity and digest

nodes.forbidden_collapse: Not a canonical registry, approved design, executable plan, or proof of complete human intent.

nodes.label: Reviewable Next Step
nodes.plain_language: The person can see what should happen next, why, what evidence supports it, and who owns it.
nodes.claim: CyberAlchemy makes the next bounded route legible instead of hiding it inside tool behavior.
nodes.scope: A desired product outcome, not a measured result.
nodes.forbidden_collapse: Not proof that the recommendation is correct and not automatic authorization to execute it.
open_questions: What observable user behavior shows that the next step was genuinely clearer?

nodes.label: Work Continuity
nodes.plain_language: Intent, evidence, decisions, tests, and ownership remain usable when work moves across time, people, or machines.
nodes.claim: The product aims to prevent important work context from disappearing between sessions and handoffs.
nodes.scope: A desired continuity outcome, not a measured customer or economic result.

source_refs.selector: ## Why IDE Ergonomics Raises The Proposition

nodes.forbidden_collapse: Not zero information loss and not a measured reduction in rework.
open_questions: Which continuity failures should become product metrics?

nodes.label: Keep Human Choice Visible
nodes.plain_language: The system may recommend or prepare, but important choices remain visible to the person responsible for them.
nodes.claim: Human indicators are opt-in, local, and reviewable, and the system does not invent human state or silently replace judgment.
nodes.scope: Product behavior involving human judgment, attention, or approval.
nodes.forbidden_collapse: Not a requirement for manual approval of every harmless operation.
open_questions: Which decisions always require explicit human choice?

nodes.label: Keep Evidence And Owner Visible
nodes.plain_language: An important recommendation, decision, or handoff should show its evidence and responsible owner.
nodes.claim: Evidence does not become authority by proximity, and ontology does not promote its own claims.
nodes.scope: Product knowledge, decisions, routes, and handoffs.
nodes.forbidden_collapse: Not a claim that cited evidence is correct or that an owner has approved the action.

nodes.label: Keep Authority Bounded And Visible
nodes.plain_language: Authority is the bounded right to make a particular consequence real, and the product must show the holder, action, target, scope, conditions, and lifecycle point.
nodes.claim: CyberAlchemy does not infer authority from participation, ownership, evidence, a recommendation, a generated artifact, a handoff, validation success, or an acceptance outside its exact envelope. Every consequential transition must use authority valid for that particular effect.
nodes.scope: Every CyberAlchemy action that can change canonical, shared, published, deployed, lifecycle, or external state.
nodes.forbidden_collapse: Not ownership, responsibility, participation, evidence, recommendation, approval preparation, test success, global permission, or a grant of authority created by this ontology record.
open_questions: Which consequence boundaries and standing authority envelopes apply to each CyberAlchemy capability?

nodes.label: Governance Serves The Work
nodes.plain_language: CyberAlchemy keeps authority, ownership, evidence, and consequence boundaries intact while using the least human-visible ceremony that preserves control.
nodes.claim: The system carries routine governance work by finding owners, preserving evidence, checking scopes, and showing prohibited effects. Reading, exploration, drafting, preview, and reversible local work remain lightweight; explicit gates appear when a transition would make work consequential.
nodes.scope: Every CyberAlchemy work loop and surface, with governance effort proportionate to the effect, reversibility, uncertainty, and authority boundary.
nodes.forbidden_collapse: Not bureaucracy, approval at every step, documentation volume, automatic safety, a replacement for product judgment, or permission to cross a consequence boundary.
open_questions: Which reversible low-effect operations may proceed under standing bounded authority without a human-interrupting gate?

nodes.label: Dynamic Human-Machine Work Fit
nodes.plain_language: CyberAlchemy must make the right governed capability available at the right moment, in a form that fits the work, the person's explicit context and attention, and the evidence and ownership boundary.
nodes.claim: The product carries avoidable memory, routing, reconstruction, and coordination burden; recognizes or accepts meaningful work moments; offers the smallest useful owner-safe choice; adapts timing, task shape, and detail through opt-in context; and preserves flow, evidence, non-action, domain priority, and human control.
nodes.scope: Every CyberAlchemy work loop and surface, from one conversation transition to persistent CLI or chat questions, session planning, handoffs, and Connective recommendations.

source_refs.selector: ## The Organizing Model: an open coordinate space (not a stack)

nodes.forbidden_collapse: Not visual polish, friction elimination, accessibility certification, hidden automation, surveillance, inferred human state, productivity scoring, comfort over domain priority, one interface for every user, or proof that a recommendation is correct.
open_questions: What evidence shows that CyberAlchemy removes avoidable burden instead of moving it elsewhere?
What evidence distinguishes a well-timed recommendation from the right task at the wrong moment?

nodes.label: Resolve Or Expose Every Required Concept
nodes.plain_language: Each required concept must have a supported decision or remain as a visible open question.
nodes.claim: Define must not silently drop a required concept or hide missing evidence behind a complete-looking pack.
nodes.scope: The product meaning of Define coverage; exact validation remains owned by Invoke.
nodes.forbidden_collapse: Not proof that open-ended human intent is complete.
open_questions: Which open questions block handoff and which may travel with the pack?

nodes.label: Resolve Context Progressively And Expose Insufficiency
nodes.plain_language: Use the context and references the person supplied first, then visible current-window and saved-session work context, and ask for more only when that bounded material is insufficient or indeterminate.
nodes.claim: Define must preserve provenance and user control while evaluating whether the available context is enough for the stated job; inferred context remains a correctable candidate and cannot silently become user intent or authority.
nodes.scope: CyberAlchemy Define context resolution for one bounded goal and named use.
nodes.forbidden_collapse: Not permission to infer private human state, treat inferred context as an answer, bypass an unresolved gap, or claim that Define already implements the evaluator.
open_questions: Which owner-adopted requirement catalog will parameterize context sufficiency for each Define job?
Which current-window boundary and retention policy will the runtime enforce?

nodes.label: Apply Bounded Language Or Expose The Gap
nodes.plain_language: Define uses exact usable language bindings and turns missing, stale, conflicting, ambiguous, or owner-unresolved language into a visible proposal or question.
nodes.claim: For one bounded Define goal, each applied language meaning is traceable to the consulted Language Context View and source digest; Define must not invent equivalence, silently choose an open realization, or drop blocked-use and owner information.
nodes.scope: Language application by Define and preservation in its Definition Pack; not general reasoning correctness or definition promotion.
nodes.owner_route: Invoke product or domain owner plus CyberAlchemy v2 Language Project owner
nodes.forbidden_collapse: Not permission to infer missing meaning, promote a definition, select an unresolved DomainSpec type, discard a language conflict, or claim correct agent interpretation.
open_questions: Which Definition Pack field will preserve the view identity, digest, and applied binding references?

nodes.label: Governance Enforcement
nodes.plain_language: Evaluate a proposed consequence against the exact owner-adopted governance constraints and authority boundary that apply, then allow or prevent that consequence without extending either boundary.
nodes.claim: CyberAlchemy treats governance enforcement as a bounded product capability: it may affect a consequence only when an applicable active rule, valid authority, and explicit enforcement binding all exist for that subject and effect.
nodes.scope: The product meaning of governance enforcement for consequential CyberAlchemy actions; runtime design, rule adoption, and surface integration remain separate.

source_refs.selector: ## First-Order Product Principles: Bounded Authority And Useful Governance

nodes.forbidden_collapse: Not an enforcement runtime, active rule, Constitution adoption, validator or gate attachment, authority grant, or proof that any repository surface is governed.
open_questions: Which product journey should first prove that an allowed consequence proceeds and a prohibited consequence is stopped without avoidable ceremony?

nodes.label: Controlled Consequences
nodes.plain_language: Consequential actions stay inside the active rule and authority boundaries that apply, while prohibited actions are stopped or routed to the responsible owner.
nodes.claim: CyberAlchemy aims to make allowed and prohibited consequences legible and to preserve those boundaries when work moves from proposal to effect.
nodes.scope: A desired product outcome for consequential work, not a claim that every effect is currently controlled.

source_refs.selector: ## First-Order Product Principles: Bounded Authority And Useful Governance

nodes.forbidden_collapse: Not zero policy violations, automatic safety, correctness proof, permission to act, or evidence that an enforcement runtime exists.
open_questions: What observations distinguish a correctly prevented consequence from an avoidable false block?
What evidence exposes a consequential action that should have been prevented but was not?

nodes.label: Only Active Rules Enforce
nodes.plain_language: A rule may affect work only when its exact version is owner-adopted, current, scoped to the matching subject, applicable to the attempted consequence, and selected by an authority-backed enforcement binding.
nodes.claim: Candidate rules, observations, evidence, assessments, policy recommendations, validations, and nearby owner records cannot block or permit work by themselves.
nodes.scope: Every CyberAlchemy enforcement decision and every integration that can change a work result or prevent a consequence.
nodes.forbidden_collapse: This ontology rule does not activate itself, adopt another rule, select an enforcement binding, grant authority, or attach governance to work.
open_questions: Which owner record and lifecycle vocabulary define active for each rule class?
Which exact adoption and enforcement-binding evidence must a future runtime require before evaluating an active rule?

nodes.plain_language: The stable work identity that keeps the PythonConstraint Goal, Research, Experiment, owners, and evidence connected.
nodes.claim: This Project coordinates one bounded CyberAlchemy-v2 and DomainSpec-v2 formal-task experiment toward the product thesis without treating the work as product proof.
nodes.scope: The private PythonConstraint whole-experiment Project record.
nodes.owner_route: CyberAlchemy v2 product owner plus DomainSpec v2 experiment owner
nodes.forbidden_collapse: Not a folder, Goal, experiment run, authority envelope, or product proof.

nodes.claim: The active Goal requires exact inputs, DomainSpec-v2 mapping, reproducible run evidence, terminal validation, and a claim-bounded product assessment.
nodes.scope: The private PythonConstraint whole-experiment Goal record; achievement is not yet proved.
nodes.owner_route: CyberAlchemy v2 product owner plus DomainSpec v2 experiment owner
nodes.forbidden_collapse: Not a plan, execution authority, progress report, or achieved result.
open_questions: Which exact DomainSpec-v2 package will satisfy success condition SC-PYC-02?

nodes.label: PythonConstraint Benchmark Admission Research
nodes.plain_language: The bounded investigation that preserves why PythonConstraint was selected and what remains unknown before a run.
nodes.claim: Pinned benchmark and source evidence supports PythonConstraint selection but not experiment execution or product effectiveness.
nodes.scope: The private Project-linked Research evidence record.
nodes.owner_route: CyberAlchemy v2 research route plus DomainSpec v2 experiment owner
nodes.forbidden_collapse: Not findings, a completed experiment, a Goal achievement decision, or authority.

nodes.owner_route: CyberAlchemy v2 experiment owner plus DomainSpec v2 experiment owner
nodes.forbidden_collapse: Not a run, finding, causal result, execution authorization, or product proof.

nodes.label: Build CyberAlchemy Systems Through DomainSpec
nodes.plain_language: Define the meaning, model the product and capability, author the system in DomainSpec v2, generate its system ontology, then build and prove against that exact model.
nodes.claim: Every new or materially revised CyberAlchemy implementation-bearing system or capability must preserve one exact chain from canonical definitions through product and business meaning, DomainSpec v2 source, deterministic compiled graph and system ontology, accepted implementation binding, and conformance evidence.
nodes.scope: CyberAlchemy v2 product construction for implementation-bearing systems and capabilities; validation utilities, receipts, migrations, and mechanical governance repairs are excluded unless they claim product or system meaning.
nodes.owner_route: CyberAlchemy v2 product ontology owner plus DomainSpec v2 construction owners
nodes.forbidden_collapse: A product rule is not a ConstructionBinding, DomainSpec source, generated system ontology, implementation admission, conformance verdict, Constitution adoption, or runtime enforcement.
open_questions: Which first bounded CyberAlchemy capability will exercise the complete construction chain?

nodes.label: Craft
nodes.plain_language: The Product inside CyberAlchemy that turns Product intent into evidence-bearing working systems.
nodes.claim: Craft is the current name of the DomainSpec v2 Product lineage and owns a draft proposition for preserving one owner-controlled chain from Product Feature and domain meaning through exact realization, construction, independent conformance, operation, recovery, and evolution.
nodes.scope: The private Craft Product identified by CA2-PRODUCT-CRAFT; DomainSpec v2 is its former name, its thesis is draft, and physical plus authority migration from legacy paths remains pending.
nodes.owner_route: Craft Product owner plus CyberAlchemy v2 product owner
nodes.forbidden_collapse: The rename does not make Product, Project, Method, Product Feature, Product Capability, public Arcanum craft capability, or .craft state one identity, and it is not proof that legacy paths already moved or that the Product creates value.
open_questions: Which first bounded Product Feature will test the Craft Product thesis?

nodes.label: Craft Product Thesis
nodes.plain_language: The draft proposition explaining why the Craft Product should exist and how evidence may require it to change.
nodes.claim: Craft should reduce repeated architecture and integration work by preserving typed continuity from Product Feature through runtime evidence and safe evolution.
nodes.scope: The draft CAV2-D63 Product Thesis for CA2-PRODUCT-CRAFT.
nodes.forbidden_collapse: Not the Product, Project, Method, Product Feature, proof of Product value, architecture selection, implementation, or adoption authority.
open_questions: Which exact owner decision will commit, revise, or reject this thesis digest?

nodes.label: Craft
nodes.plain_language: The stable coordination identity for developing and evolving the Craft Product.
nodes.claim: The Craft Project connects the Product, Method, Goals, owners, evidence, decisions, artifacts, migration work, and residue without owning their separate authority.
nodes.scope: The proposed CAV2-D60 Project identified by CA2-PROJECT-CRAFT.
nodes.forbidden_collapse: Not the Craft Product, Craft Method, Project folder, Goal, Product Feature, implementation, or authority envelope.

nodes.label: Craft Method
nodes.plain_language: CyberAlchemy's repeatable way to carry Product intent through exact construction, checking, operation, recovery, evolution, and owner continuation.
nodes.claim: The Craft Method is the governed recursive system-building method embodied by the Craft Product and used by the Craft Project; ledgering preserves continuity but is not the whole method.
nodes.scope: The active canonical CAV2-D20 Method definition and its private CyberAlchemy domain context.
nodes.forbidden_collapse: Not the Craft Product, Craft Project, Product Thesis, Product Feature, DomainSpec model, generator, runtime, public Arcanum craft capability, or .craft ledger state.
open_questions: Which first bounded Product Feature will exercise every required Method stage?
